mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 2.0% for two consecutive months signals central bank over-tightening, which raises real discount rates and dampens equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.0% and remains above for ≥2 consecutive months
regime_hint: accelerating inflation in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Over the 20-day horizon, SPX 20d returns are not statistically different from the prior month's return (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL reverts below 2.0% within one month.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in a single month, the expected discount rate on future earnings rises, depressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) during the identified FEDFUNDS hike month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS of at least 2,000 jobs over three months indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2,000 monthly for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are negative or flat during the identified labor expansion period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS falls by more than 10% in a month, it signals a sharp contraction in corporate credit demand, which reduces expected future earnings and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >10% in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive and statistically significant during the RSAFS decline episode (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (below -3.0 index points) suggests weakening manufacturing capacity utilization, which raises supply-side uncertainty and can depress equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >3.0 index points in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are not statistically different from the prior month (t-test p > 0.05) during the INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in HOUST of at least 5% for two months reflect accelerating consumer demand, which elevates earnings growth expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns remain negative or flat despite the identified HOUST expansion (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1.50% for three consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime, it suggests policy accommodation, lowering real rates and supporting equity valuations, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.50% for three consecutive months and macro regime is non-recessionary
evidence_refs: fact:non-recessionary regime as defined by GDP growth > 2% and unemployment < 4%
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are negative or flat during the identified accommodation period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both GDPC1 (demand) and a decline in UNRATE (labor cost pressure) creates a dual signal of robust demand and wage restraint, which together lower real wage growth and support equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases and UNRATE decreases over the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative during episodes matching the GDPC1/UNRATE interaction pattern (t-test p > 0.05).
